title: Sunset Session

conditions.headline: Fed holds the line, small swell rolls to the beach
conditions.summary: Stocks edged higher after the Fed held rates in a 10-2 vote with two hawkish dissents. Oracle's big outlook lifted tech while yields climbed to 5.05%.

sections.title: Closing Bell
items: Russell 2000 gained 0.41% to 2,830.51.
Stocks held modest gains after the Fed's rate hold, with Oracle's long-range outlook boosting tech.
Technology (+0.8%), financials and energy led; utilities (-0.8%), real estate and communication services lagged.
VIX eased 3.5% to 16.91.

sections.title: Macro & Fed
items: Fed held rates at 3.75%-4.00% in a 10-2 vote; Lisa Cook and Beth Hammack dissented in favor of a hike.
The statement said the economy is expanding at a strong pace and inflation remains elevated.
Chair Kevin Warsh said 2027 will have one fewer policy meeting, replaced by a strategy-only session.
Traders see roughly 85% odds of a quarter-point hike on Dec. 9.
10-year yield rose about 5 bp to 5.05%; crude rose 1.8% to about $101.67 after an attack on a Saudi refinery.
Gold was flat near $4,075; bitcoin rose 0.6% to about $81,100.

sections.title: Biggest Movers
items: ORCL (Oracle): +10.7% — projected fiscal 2030 revenue of at least $225 billion.
VRT (Vertiv): +17% — sales up 61% and a $650 million lift to its full-year sales forecast.
SK hynix (US shares): +13% — operating profit up more than sixfold; sees memory shortages into 2030.
WEN (Wendy's): +14% to +15% — confirmed a $7.35-a-share take-private proposal from a Trian-led group.
FFIV (F5): -20% — slower fiscal 2027 revenue forecast.
ENPH (Enphase): -17% — weak residential solar demand and a soft Q4 outlook.
CSGP (CoStar): -15% — fell after its quarterly report.
LOGI (Logitech): -12% — flagged a $70 million to $80 million hit from a plant incident.

sections.title: Earnings Today & Tonight
items: Microsoft beat: EPS $4.89 vs $4.73 expected, revenue $92.3B vs $90.6B; shares up about 4% after hours.
Alphabet: revenue $111.2B, just below estimates, EPS $2.12 vs $2.99 expected; shares down about 8.7% after hours.
Fortinet fell after hours; Chipotle, ServiceNow, Ford and Carvana also reported after the close.
Before the open: Vertiv +17%, Flex +11%, Amphenol +3%, GE Vernova -1%; Boston Scientific fell about 11% early.

sections.title: Business News
items: Trian and partners made a non-binding $7.35-a-share cash proposal to take Wendy's private.
Anthropic's IPO filing drew attention to AI infrastructure and natural gas demand.
Banks are lining up $21 billion in debt for a Broadcom chip deal.
Goldman Sachs expects US data-center electricity demand to double from 2025 to 2027.
An attack on a Saudi refinery pushed crude back above $100.

sections.title: On Deck
items: 7:30 AM CT: Q3 GDP, September PCE and core PCE, personal income and spending, weekly jobless claims.
Before the open: Eli Lilly, Mastercard, Merck, Caterpillar, Linde, Bristol Myers Squibb.
After the close: Amazon, Intel, Gilead, Starbucks, Coinbase, Stryker.
No Fed speakers listed on the calendar.

Cowabunga! This is Surf Daddy, your local Kahuna, live from Surfside USA to all you Trade Wind surfers from the Gulf Coast to the North Shore. It's Wednesday, October twenty-eighth, twenty twenty-six, and this is your Sunset Session, the full wrap of today's market. The sun is sliding down into the water, the last set is rolling in, and the board is waxed for tomorrow.

Gus the wonder dog spent the whole Fed meeting with his ears up, waiting on the big announcement. Give the crew a sunset howdy, Gus! [BARK]

Here's the final set. Stocks drifted higher into the close after the Fed sat tight on rates. The S and P five hundred rose about three tenths of a percent to seven thousand seven hundred forty-four. The Nasdaq added about three tenths of a percent to twenty-six thousand five hundred fifty. The Dow gained about two tenths of a percent to fifty-two thousand four hundred seventy-five. Small caps did a touch better. Tech led the sectors, while utilities and real estate lagged.

Now the wind and weather. The Fed held its key rate at three and three quarters to four percent, as expected. But the vote was ten to two, and both dissenters, Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack, wanted a rate hike. Traders now see about an eighty-five percent chance of a quarter point hike on December ninth. The ten year Treasury yield rose about five basis points to five point zero five percent. Oil climbed almost two percent to about one hundred one dollars and sixty-seven cents after an attack on a Saudi refinery. Gold was flat.

Let's check the lineup. Oracle was the Kahuna of the big names, up almost eleven percent after projecting at least two hundred twenty-five billion dollars in revenue for fiscal twenty thirty. That's a wave ridden all the way to the sand. Gus, that's worth a biscuit! Here you go, buddy! [SNACK] Vertiv surged about seventeen percent on a sixty-one percent jump in sales and a higher forecast. On the wipeout side, F five sank about twenty percent on a slower revenue outlook, Enphase dropped about seventeen percent on weak solar demand.

Over on the tide chart, Microsoft beat on earnings, revenue and cloud, and the stock rose about four percent after hours. Alphabet's revenue was a hair light and profit missed, and shares fell about eight and a half percent late. This morning, Flex rose about eleven percent after its report.

Beach talk. Trian made a take-private offer for Wendy's at seven dollars and thirty-five cents a share, and the stock jumped about fifteen percent. Anthropic's I P O filing put a spotlight on A I data centers and the power they need.

Tomorrow's forecast is a big swell. At seven thirty A M Central we get third quarter G D P, September P C E inflation, personal income and spending, and jobless claims. Before the open, Eli Lilly, Mastercard, Merck and Caterpillar report. After the close, it's Amazon, Intel, Gilead, Starbucks and Coinbase. Hang ten through it, and no kook moves.

Catch the Dawn Patrol tomorrow morning before the bell. And hey, want me to call a wave for you? Type any stock, E T F or futures contract into the Check a Wave box on the page, and Surf Daddy will call it.

This is information, not advice. This is Surf Daddy and Gus the wonder dog saying, if in doubt, paddle out!
